title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Carlos E. Jimenez; John Yang; Alexander Wettig; Shunyu Yao; Kexin Pei; Ofir Press; Karthik Narasimhan
central_claim: 2,294 issue-resolution tasks from 12 Python repos; best model then (Claude 2) resolved 1.96%.
cite_claim: Foundational issue-resolution benchmark whose success criterion is passing developer tests tied to the fix.
quote: Claude 2 is able to solve a mere 1.96% of the issues
relevance: Defines the test-based success metric whose weaknesses (plausible != correct) we must avoid repeating.

title: SWE-bench Verified (dataset card)
authors: princeton-nlp / SWE-bench team; human validation by OpenAI
central_claim: 500-instance human-validated subset; FAIL_TO_PASS tests tied to the issue, PASS_TO_PASS tests must pass before and after.
cite_claim: F2P/P2P definitions we mirror: fiks's repro is an F2P test; prior traces + contract suite play the P2P role.
quote: a subset of 500 samples from the SWE-bench test set, which have been human-validated for quality
relevance: Vocabulary for our F and P gates; the OpenAI blog describing validation returned 403 [verify].

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
authors: John Yang; Carlos E. Jimenez; Alexander Wettig; Kilian Lieret; Shunyu Yao; Karthik Narasimhan; Ofir Press
central_claim: A purpose-built agent-computer interface lets an LM agent edit repos and run tests; 12.5% pass@1 on SWE-bench.
cite_claim: Canonical agentic repair scaffold; candidate ungated baseline (bash agent on the target repo given an issue).
quote: achieving state-of-the-art performance on both with a pass@1 rate of 12.5% and 87.7%
relevance: Baseline candidate (SWE-agent / mini-swe-agent) for issue-text-only repair.

title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
authors: Chunqiu Steven Xia; Yinlin Deng; Soren Dunn; Lingming Zhang
central_claim: A fixed localize-repair-validate pipeline reaches 32.00% on SWE-bench Lite at $0.70; generated reproduction tests plus regression tests are the largest filtering gain.
cite_claim: Patch validation by an LLM-generated reproduction test raised fixes from 81 to 96 on Lite (Table 4); some benchmark issues contain the exact patch (4.3%) or a misleading one (5.0%).
quote: Agentless employs a simplistic three-phase process of localization, repair, and patch validation
relevance: Closest pipeline analogue of fiks's reproduce+validate; its repro test is guessed from prose, ours is captured from traffic.

title: AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement
authors: Yuntong Zhang; Haifeng Ruan; Zhiyu Fan; Abhik Roychoudhury
central_claim: Program-structure-aware code search plus spectrum-based fault localization; ~19% of SWE-bench Lite at ~$0.43 per issue.
cite_claim: Representative structure-aware LLM repair agent.
quote: We posit that our workflow enables autonomous software engineering
relevance: Related work; Python-specific so not a direct baseline on TS servers.

title: SpecRover: Code Intent Extraction via LLMs
authors: Haifeng Ruan; Yuntong Zhang; Abhik Roychoudhury
central_claim: Iterative specification inference plus a reviewer agent that vets patches and gives a confidence signal; >50% efficacy gain over AutoCodeRover on full SWE-bench.
cite_claim: Prior work also infers intent/specs to vet patches, but from code and issue text, not from runtime contracts.
quote: is examined by a reviewer agent with the goal of vetting the patches
relevance: Strongest competing idea for 'spec-guided acceptance'; fiks's contracts are explicit and executable rather than LLM-inferred.

title: RepairAgent: An Autonomous, LLM-Based Agent for Program Repair
authors: Islem Bouzenia; Premkumar Devanbu; Michael Pradel
central_claim: Tool-using LLM agent repairs 164 Defects4J bugs (39 not fixed before) at ~270k tokens / ~14 cents per bug.
cite_claim: First autonomous LLM agent for test-driven program repair.
quote: repairing 164 bugs, including 39 bugs not fixed by prior techniques
relevance: Agentic APR lineage; Defects4J correctness is judged against developer patches.

title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
authors: Xingyao Wang et al. (24 authors, incl. Graham Neubig)
central_claim: MIT-licensed open platform for coding agents evaluated on 15 benchmarks including SWE-bench.
cite_claim: Open, MIT-licensed agent platform usable as a third-party repair baseline.
quote: a platform for the development of powerful and flexible AI agents
relevance: Runnable baseline (MIT) for issue-only repair on shop-mcp forks.

title: Are "Solved Issues" in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly? An Empirical Study
authors: You Wang; Michael Pradel; Zhongxin Liu
central_claim: Running all developer tests shows 7.8% of 'plausible' patches fail; differential testing (PatchDiff) finds 29.6% of plausible patches behave differently from the reference; ~28.6% of inspected divergent patches are certainly incorrect; resolution rates inflated by 6.2 points.
cite_claim: Plausible patches are often not correct; differential testing against a reference patch plus manual review is a practical correctness check.
location: Abstract; Sec. 3.2 (PatchDiff); Sec. 4.1-4.4 (RQ1-RQ4); 6.2 pts in abstract vs 6.4 in Sec. 4.4
quote: which causes 7.8% of all patches to count as "correct" while failing the developer-written test suite
relevance: Deep-read. Method to borrow for evaluating fiks patches (differential tests vs a reference fix per drift).

title: SWE-Bench+: Enhanced Coding Benchmark for LLMs
authors: Reem Aleithan; Haoran Xue; Mohammad Mahdi Mohajer; Elijah Nnorom; Gias Uddin; Song Wang
central_claim: 32.67% of successful SWE-agent+GPT-4 patches had the solution in the issue or comments; 31.08% passed only because tests were weak; filtering drops 12.47% to 3.97%.
cite_claim: Solution leakage and weak tests inflate repair success; a fair evaluation must control what the agent is told.
quote: solutions were directly provided in the issue report or the comments
relevance: Deep-read. Strongest reviewer analogy: a fiks trace that shows the raw upstream field may 'leak' the fix.

title: UTBoost: Rigorous Evaluation of Coding Agents on SWE-Bench
authors: Boxi Yu; Yuxuan Zhu; Pinjia He; Daniel Kang
central_claim: LLM-augmented test generation found 36 instances with insufficient tests and 345 erroneous patches marked passing; 24.4% of Verified leaderboard entries affected.
cite_claim: Benchmark tests are insufficient; augmenting them with generated tests changes rankings.
quote: insufficient, allowing generated patches to pass the tests without resolving the underlying issue
relevance: Supports augmenting the gate with held-out generated tests.

title: The SWE-Bench Illusion: When State-of-the-Art LLMs Remember Instead of Reason
authors: Shanchao Liang; Spandan Garg; Roshanak Zilouchian Moghaddam
central_claim: Models identify buggy file paths from issue text alone with up to 76% accuracy on SWE-bench Verified vs up to 53% on other repos, suggesting memorization.
cite_claim: Contamination may inflate SWE-bench Verified scores.
quote: performance gains on SWE-Bench-Verified may be partially driven by memorization rather than genuine problem-solving
relevance: Argues for fresh, unseen bugs; fiks's seeded drifts are uncontaminated but self-authored.

title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
authors: Ibragim Badertdinov et al. (Nebius)
central_claim: Continuously mined fresh tasks give a decontaminated benchmark; some models' Verified scores look inflated.
cite_claim: Fresh-task evaluation is the accepted remedy for contamination.
quote: static benchmarks quickly become outdated due to contamination issues
relevance: Template for a time-split real-bug set.

title: SWE-bench Goes Live!
authors: Linghao Zhang; Shilin He; Chaoyun Zhang; et al.
central_claim: 1,319 post-2024 tasks across 93 repos with Docker images; agents score noticeably lower than on static SWE-bench.
cite_claim: Agents perform worse on fresh tasks than on static SWE-bench.
quote: a live-updatable benchmark designed to overcome these challenges
relevance: Supports reporting real-bug results separately from seeded drifts.

title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
authors: Xiang Deng; Jeff Da; Edwin Pan; et al. (Scale AI)
central_claim: 1,865 human-verified tasks from 41 repos with public, held-out and commercial splits to resist contamination.
cite_claim: Held-out splits are used to resist contamination.
quote: Problems in the held-out and the commercial set are not publicly accessible
relevance: Model for keeping a held-out drift/bug split unseen during fiks development.

title: TDFlow: Agentic Workflows for Test Driven Development
authors: Kevin Han; Siddharth Maddikayala; Tim Knappe; Om Patel; Austen Liao; Amir Barati Farimani
central_claim: Given human-written reproduction tests, issue resolution reaches 94.3% on SWE-bench Verified vs 68.0% with LLM-generated tests; test hacking was rare (3 of 400 on Verified).
cite_claim: The bottleneck is writing a true reproduction test (existing C17). Note: intro gives 69.8% for the LLM-test mode; Table 2 gives 68.0%.
quote: the primary obstacle to human-level software engineering performance lies within writing successful reproduction tests
relevance: Deep-read. Core support for C17/C19; also a caution: tests used both to guide and to grade (no held-out set).

title: SWE-Doctor: Guiding Software Engineering Agents with Runtime Diagnosis from Multi-Faceted Bug Reproduction Tests
authors: Yaoqi Guo; Yang Liu; Jie M. Zhang; Yun Ma; Yiling Lou; Zhenpeng Chen
central_claim: Single fail-to-pass reproduction tests give limited or negative gains because they cover one manifestation; multi-faceted tests plus runtime diagnosis reach 75.7% Verified / 59.4% Pro.
cite_claim: F2P tests can lead to partial patches (existing C20).
quote: fail-to-pass BRTs may cover only one manifestation of the reported issue, leading to partial patches
relevance: Direct counter-evidence to 'one repro test is enough'; motivates fiks's full contract suite + all-trace gate.

title: SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents
authors: Niels Mundler; Mark Niklas Muller; Jingxuan He; Martin Vechev
central_claim: Generated issue-reproduction tests filter code fixes, more than doubling SWE-agent precision to 47.8% at ~20% recall cost.
cite_claim: Using F2P tests as an acceptance filter raises precision and lowers recall.
quote: this more than doubles the precision of SWE-Agent to 47.8%
relevance: Precision/recall framing for comparing gated vs ungated repair.

title: Otter: Generating Tests from Issues to Validate SWE Patches
authors: Toufique Ahmed; Jatin Ganhotra; Rangeet Pan; Avraham Shinnar; Saurabh Sinha; Martin Hirzel
central_claim: Issue-to-test generation produces fail-to-pass tests for 31.4% (Otter) / 37% (Otter++) of TDD-Bench-Verified instances; filtering leaderboard patches gives 65-92% precision at 30-41% recall.
cite_claim: Even the best issue-to-test generators produce a valid F2P test for only about a third of instances.
quote: Otter augments LLMs with rule-based analysis to check and repair their outputs
relevance: Baseline rate for 'LLM writes the repro from prose' vs fiks capturing it from traffic.

title: ImpossibleBench: Measuring LLMs' Propensity of Exploiting Test Cases
authors: Ziqian Zhong; Aditi Raghunathan; Nicholas Carlini
central_claim: On spec-vs-test conflicting SWE-bench tasks, GPT-5 cheats 54.0%; hiding tests nearly eliminates cheating, read-only tests block test edits but not special-casing.
cite_claim: Coding agents exploit tests (deleting/editing tests, special-casing); read-only tests are a partial mitigation.
quote: an LLM agent with access to unit tests may delete failing tests rather than fix the underlying bug
relevance: Justifies fiks's edit allow-list (src only) and argues for a held-out oracle the agent never sees.

title: Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
authors: Theo X. Olausson; Jeevana Priya Inala; Chenglong Wang; Jianfeng Gao; Armando Solar-Lezama
central_claim: Self-repair gains are modest once cost is counted; bottlenecked by feedback quality; stronger feedback helps substantially.
cite_claim: Repair quality is limited by the quality of the feedback signal.
quote: self-repair is bottlenecked by the model's ability to provide feedback on its own code
relevance: Supports the thesis that a precise violation signal (trace + property) is what makes repair work.

title: Evaluating Agent-based Program Repair at Google
authors: Pat Rondon; Renyao Wei; Jose Cambronero; Jurgen Cito; Aaron Sun; Siddhant Sanyam; Michele Tufano; Satish Chandra
central_claim: On 178 Google bugs, Passerine made plausible patches for 73% of machine-reported and 25.6% of human-reported bugs, but only 43% / 17.9% were semantically equivalent to the ground truth by manual review.
cite_claim: In industry, plausible (test-passing) and valid (equivalent to developer fix) rates diverge sharply; machine-reported bugs with crisp repro signals are far more repairable.
location: Abstract; Sec. III-C; Sec. IV; Table IV; Sec. V-A
quote: We determine this correctness through manual analysis performed by three of the authors.
relevance: Deep-read. Machine-reported (sanitizer/flaky) bugs are the closest analogue to fiks's machine-detected violations; plausible-vs-valid protocol to copy.

title: Agentic Program Repair from Test Failures at Scale: A Neuro-symbolic approach with static analysis and test execution feedback
authors: Chandra Maddila; Adam Tait; et al. (Meta)
central_claim: A Meta agent triggered by failing tests reaches 42.3% SR@1 offline; in production (Feb-Apr 2025) 1,589 fixes published, 80% reviewed, 31.5% of reviewed landed.
cite_claim: Industrial repair triggered by machine-detected failures, gated by test pass + LLM judge + CI, still needs human review; most reviewed fixes are not landed.
location: Sec. III, VIII-B Table III, VIII-C Table IV, IX Table V, IX-B
quote: Of those that received a review, 31.5% were accepted.
relevance: Deep-read. Closest industrial analogue of fiks's Repair+Ship steps; reasons for rejection (partial fixes, missing context) predict our failure modes.

title: AI-powered patching: the future of automated vulnerability fixes
authors: Jan Keller; Jan Nowakowski
central_claim: Gemini fixed 15% of sanitizer bugs found during unit tests; fixes are produced for human review.
cite_claim: Industrial LLM repair of machine-detected (sanitizer) bugs keeps humans in the review loop.
quote: harnessed our Gemini model to successfully fix 15% of sanitizer bugs discovered during unit tests
relevance: Industrial precedent: detector-triggered repair, human-reviewed.

title: Finding and fixing software bugs automatically with SapFix and Sapienz
authors: Facebook/Meta Engineering
central_claim: SapFix generates fixes for crashes found by Sapienz, validates with developer and Sapienz tests, and proposes them to engineers; it does not deploy fixes on its own.
cite_claim: First end-to-end detect-test-repair pipeline at industrial scale, with mandatory human approval.
quote: is not designed to deploy fixes to production code on its own
relevance: Closest historical precedent for fiks's 'never auto-merge' design; the ICSE-SEIP 2019 paper is the citable version [verify DOI].

title: Getafix: Learning to Fix Bugs Automatically
authors: Johannes Bader; Andrew Scott; Michael Pradel; Satish Chandra
central_claim: Learns fix patterns from human fixes for static-analysis warnings; top suggestion matches human fix 12-91% by category; deployed at Facebook.
cite_claim: Industrial repair driven by a machine detector (static analyzer) rather than by issue prose.
quote: Getafix is the first industrially-deployed automated bug-fixing tool
relevance: Detector-triggered repair precedent; fixes match human fixes as the correctness proxy.

title: Human-competitive Patches in Automatic Program Repair with Repairnator
authors: Martin Monperrus; Simon Urli; Thomas Durieux; Matias Martinez; Benoit Baudry; Lionel Seinturier
central_claim: A bot monitoring CI build failures in OSS produced patches that maintainers accepted and merged.
cite_claim: Program-repair bots that open PRs from CI failures have been accepted by human maintainers.
quote: Repairnator is a bot. It constantly monitors software bugs discovered during continuous integration of open-source software
relevance: Closest open-source precedent for 'failure signal -> repair -> PR'; trigger is an existing failing test, not a silent runtime violation.

title: How to Design a Program Repair Bot? Insights from the Repairnator Project
authors: Simon Urli; Zhongxing Yu; Lionel Seinturier; Martin Monperrus
central_claim: Over 11,317 test failures in 1,609 GitHub projects, the bot generated patches for 17 bugs.
cite_claim: Repair bots driven by CI test failures yield low patch rates in the wild.
quote: The Repairnator bot is an autonomous agent that constantly monitors test failures
relevance: Base-rate realism for real-bug runs.

title: An Analysis of Patch Plausibility and Correctness for Generate-and-Validate Patch Generation Systems
authors: Zichao Qi; Fan Long; Sara Achour; Martin Rinard
central_claim: Most patches reported by GenProg, RSRepair and AE are not plausible, and the overwhelming majority are not correct, often equivalent to deleting functionality; Kali (deletion only) does as well.
cite_claim: Origin of the plausible-vs-correct distinction; test-validated patches often just delete functionality.
quote: The overwhelming majority of the reported patches are not correct and are equivalent to a single modification that simply deletes functionality.
relevance: Foundational for C20-style risk; a 'delete the check' fix must fail fiks's gates.

title: Is the Cure Worse Than the Disease? Overfitting in Automated Program Repair
authors: Edward K. Smith; Earl T. Barr; Claire Le Goues; Yuriy Brun
central_claim: Evaluating patches with tests independent of those used for repair shows GenProg/TrpAutoRepair overfit; patch quality tracks repair test-suite coverage.
cite_claim: Patch correctness must be measured on held-out tests independent of the tests used to construct the patch.
quote: one test suite is training data used to construct a patch, and the other is evaluation or held-out data
relevance: Methodological anchor for a held-out oracle in fiks's evaluation.

title: Identifying Patch Correctness in Test-Based Program Repair
authors: Yingfei Xiong; Xinyuan Liu; Muhan Zeng; Lu Zhang; Gang Huang
central_claim: Generating new inputs and comparing test behavior on original vs patched programs filtered 56.3% of incorrect patches with no correct ones lost (139 patches).
cite_claim: Automated test generation + behavioral comparison can screen overfitting patches.
quote: Our approach successfully prevented 56.3% of the incorrect patches to be generated, without blocking any correct patches.
relevance: Precedent for differential checks against the original program.

title: Automatically Patching Errors in Deployed Software
authors: Jeff H. Perkins; Sunghun Kim; Sam Larsen; Saman Amarasinghe; et al.; Michael D. Ernst; Martin Rinard
central_claim: ClearView learns invariants from normal runs (Daikon), detects failures with monitors, patches binaries by enforcing violated invariants, and keeps the patch that works; in a Red Team exercise it blocked all 10 exploits and auto-patched 7.
cite_claim: Earliest closed loop of learned invariants -> runtime violation -> automatic patch -> evaluation in production.
quote: observes normal executions to learn invariants that characterize the application's normal behavior
relevance: Strongest prior-art for the 'observe invariants then repair' loop; differs from fiks by hot-patching binaries without humans or source PRs.

title: Enhancing Server Availability and Security Through Failure-Oblivious Computing
authors: Martin Rinard; Cristian Cadar; Daniel Dumitran; Daniel M. Roy; Tudor Leu; William S. Beebee Jr.
central_claim: Discarding invalid writes and manufacturing values for invalid reads lets servers keep serving through memory errors.
cite_claim: Classical runtime self-healing masks errors to preserve availability rather than fixing code.
quote: enables servers to execute through memory errors without memory corruption
relevance: Contrast: masking at runtime (like a receipt-only monitor) vs durable source fix.

title: Automatic Software Repair: a Bibliography
authors: Martin Monperrus
central_claim: Distinguishes behavioral repair (change code; oracle = tests, contracts, crashing inputs) from state repair (runtime recovery).
cite_claim: Taxonomy: fiks's receipts are state/runtime mitigation; its PRs are behavioral repair with contracts as the oracle.
quote: Automatic software repair consists of automatically finding a solution to software bugs without human intervention.
relevance: Framing for positioning fiks across both repair families.
